paper.title: DoReMi: Grounding Language Model by Detecting and Recovering from Plan-Execution Misalignment
paper.central_claim: Using an LLM both to plan and to generate execution constraints, and a VLM to continuously detect constraint violations, lets robot arms and humanoids immediately detect and recover from plan-execution misalignment, giving higher task success and shorter completion time.

provenance.expectations_note: no standalone expectations file; E01-E22 are embedded in patterns/main/*.md

evidence.quote: a novel language model grounding framework that enables immediate Detection and Recovery from Misalignments between plan and execution
However, these grounding methods often assume that every low-level skill can perfectly execute the high-level plan generated by the language model.
However, Inner Monologue needs manually designed queries to get information from environments, which is impractical and hard to obtain at high frequency.
If so, the robot continues executing the current low-level skill; otherwise, the robot aborts the current skill, and the re-planning process is triggered.
Practically, we deploy the Vicuna-13B model
evidence.support_explanation: Planner backbone for results; GPT-4 only mentioned.

evidence.quote: We also try GPT4 [ 42 ] through OpenAI API to directly output the next step with zero temperature.
evidence.support_explanation: GPT-4 tried but no results reported.

evidence.quote: We observe that pre-trained zero-shot VLM can perform well in most tasks, except those with extremely complex scenes.
The dataset only consisted of 128 image-text pairs with 5 demonstrations on fruit objects.
evidence.support_explanation: Fine-tune data size and overlap risk.

evidence.quote: The max execution time for all tasks is set to 20 seconds. Any execution that takes time longer than 20 seconds is considered as failure.
The results show the mean and standard deviation over 4 different seeds, each with 12 episodes.
evidence.support_explanation: Table I denominators: 4 seeds x 12 episodes.

evidence.quote: IM-Oracle: Inner-Monologue with oracle feedback which does not exist in practical real-world settings.
However, they do not have a mechanism to abort the current execution and only re-plan at the end of each skill, resulting in a longer execution time.
Under these two mechanisms, DoReMi reaches higher success rates and shorter execution times.
Furthermore, DoReMi-FT even surpasses IM-oracle in execution time while maintaining similar success rates due to its immediate detection and recovery mechanism
evidence.support_explanation: Immediacy effect separated from feedback accuracy via oracle.
Real humanoid success percentages (IM, DoReMi, DoReMi-FT); trial counts absent.
Detector confusion counts before/after fine-tune (humanoid tasks).
Zero-shot VLM ablation success (BLIP-1/BLIP-2/Instruct-BLIP) on prepare-food.

evidence.quote: The LLMs and VLMs are running on the cloud and communicate with the robot at 1Hz.
We assume the block has a probability p to drop every second when sucked by the end-effector

signatures.object: plan step + LLM-generated constraints checked continuously by a VLM binary detector during low-level skill execution
signatures.information: LLM sees instruction, previous skills and violation notes; VLM sees camera image and 'Is the constraint satisfied?' question; sim success by environment; IM-Oracle baseline gets oracle feedback
signatures.operation: LLM picks next skill (argmax over skills) and emits constraints; every 0.2 s BLIP-2 answers Yes/No per constraint; first violation aborts the skill and triggers replanning with violation text in the prompt
signatures.conditions: constraints expressible as visual Yes/No; detector accuracy adequate; synthetic disturbances (drop, noise, obstacles, pick failure)
signatures.feedback: VLM verdicts (learned, not ground truth) + LLM replanning
signatures.selection_rule_data: any False verdict -> abort and replan; no ensembling or confirmation
signatures.persistence: violation info appended to prompt within the episode
signatures.later_use: next planning call in the episode
signatures.claimed_effect: higher success and shorter time than SayCan/CLIPort/Inner Monologue
signatures.failure_boundary: complex scenes degrade zero-shot VLM (prepare-food 37-40%); constraint correctness unchecked

signatures.object: LoRA fine-tune of BLIP-2 on 128 image-text pairs (DoReMi-FT)
signatures.information: Small humanoid-scene dataset with fruit objects
signatures.operation: parameter-efficient fine-tune of the constraint detector
signatures.output: detector with higher TP/lower FN on humanoid tasks
signatures.conditions: single A100; evaluation tasks may overlap fine-tune scenes
signatures.claimed_effect: prepare-food success 37% -> 91% (sim); generalizes to unseen objects/backgrounds/tasks (qualitative)
signatures.failure_boundary: generalization shown qualitatively; overlap not controlled

gap.author_gap: Hierarchical LLM grounding assumes skills execute plans perfectly; feedback after each step is late and Inner Monologue needs manually designed queries and cannot run at high frequency.
gap.checked_gap: Real and specific (delayed feedback, ambiguous open-ended scene descriptions) and quantified against the nearest neighbour in the paper (IM, IM-Oracle). Execution-monitoring literature outside LLM planners is not discussed.

lineage_closest_adjacent.name: Inner Monologue (IM)
lineage_closest_adjacent.solved: success detectors and scene descriptors fed back to LLM after each step

gap.residue: VLM accuracy in complex scenes, correctness of LLM-generated constraints, real-world trial counts, latency and call cost.
gap.stakes: SayCan fails under disturbance; IM recovers late or not at all (e.g. 40-68% vs 90-95% with obstacle/drop disturbances).
gap.method_response: LLM writes task-specific constraints; VLM answers binary questions continuously; violation triggers replanning.
gap.remaining_gap: Complex-scene detector reliability, non-visual constraints, real trials and cost.
unresolved: Lineage beyond IM/SayCan/CLIPort not pinned locally.

matches.reason: LLM output is split into a plan step and a checkable constraint object routed to a VLM verifier whose verdict gates control; differs from C25 in that the 'solver' is a learned VLM and no soundness is claimed.

rs_pattern.reason: Primary chosen by operation (constraint artifact verified externally, loop closed during execution). assumption_audit_and_pivot was read (the 'skills execute plans' assumption) but the paper builds a mechanism, not a relaxed guarantee or exploit.

executes_pattern.reason: Handoff artifact and in-loop verification executed; mechanism isolation and cost accounting incomplete.

resolves_problem.reason: Closes late-detection gap under injected disturbances in simulation; real-world and complex-scene reliability not established.

condition_checks.note: Completion/violation monitor audited via TP/FN/FP/TN on humanoid tasks (Table III) but not for Ravens tasks
Detector false positives/negatives non-zero (e.g. prepare food FN 27 before FT); sim detector is a learned VLM, not privileged
Constraint generation and continuous polling not isolated
Executor fidelity (CLIPort/DeepMimic skills) held fixed; not varied

matches.reason: Executor runs until a monitor fires then control returns to the planner; the monitor here is a stagnation-free constraint check (violation), not a completion check, and it aborts the running skill.

unassigned.operation: LLM-generated, skill-specific constraints turned into binary VQA queries for the monitor
unassigned.reason: K202 does not cover how monitor conditions are authored by the planner.

revision_proposals.title: K202 variant: planner-authored constraint monitor aborting running skills
revision_proposals.support: single paper (2307.00329); needs a second independent full text

pattern_mapping.operation_correspondence: Structured artifact (constraint) handed to an external checker whose verdict gates the learned executor and triggers replanning ~ monitor fires and control returns to planner.
pattern_mapping.necessary_conditions_and_differences: C25 expects a sound solver; here a learned VLM, so reliability is an empirical question (Table III). K202 monitors completion/stagnation; DoReMi monitors violation of planner-authored invariants.

assessment.evidence_level_reason: Closed-loop simulation (arm and humanoid) with environment-judged success and 4x12-episode repeats; real humanoid reported without trial counts. Two embodiments exist, but harness prompts, disturbances and detector fine-tune were built on the same tasks (EVIDENCE rule 2) and the real results lack counts, so no transfer credit.
assessment.strongest_supported_claim: Under author-injected disturbances in simulation, planner-authored constraints with continuous VLM checking and replanning beat SayCan, CLIPort and Inner Monologue on success and time with Vicuna-13B and BLIP-2; real-world gains and generality to other planners/scenes are indicative only.
unresolved: constraint generation vs continuous polling not isolated

G.reason: Specific bottleneck (late/ambiguous feedback; assumption of perfect skill execution) with the nearest neighbour reimplemented and an oracle bound; execution-monitoring lineage outside LLM planners and real-world stakes only sketched; residual (complex scenes) stated.

M.reason: Reasoning is reconstructable (focused binary questions reduce VLM ambiguity; continuous polling saves time) and yields distinguishable predictions (time gap vs IM-Oracle); assumptions (LLM constraints correct, visually decidable) untested.

X.reason: Algorithm 1, polling period, models and example pipeline given; real humanoid loop at 1 Hz stated; missing: full prompt p0, constraint-correctness checks, IM baseline implementation details, per-cell n in Table II, fine-tune split.

measurement.reason: Sim success judged by environment with 20 s cap, Table I n=48 per cell with std, oracle bound and a detector confusion table (humanoid); gaps: Table II n and real trial counts absent, detector not audited for Ravens, disturbances synthetic.

causality.reason: Matched LLM/VLM across baselines, IM-Oracle separates feedback accuracy from immediacy (DoReMi-FT faster than oracle), VLM variants ablated; unseparated: constraint generation vs continuous polling, single planner backbone.

holdout.reason: Disturbances and tasks authored for the method; fine-tune set (128 pairs, fruit) vs prepare-food overlap uncontrolled; unseen-object generalization is qualitative; no held-out planner or embodiment beyond the two shown tasks sets.

statistics.reason: Mean+std over 4 seeds x 12 episodes in Table I, detector TP/FN/FP/TN, success by disturbance level; no paired tests; Table II/real n unstated.

cost.reason: Execution time and detector latency (<0.1 s query, 0.2 s period, 1 Hz real loop) given and baselines share LLM/VLM; VLM query counts, LLM calls, compute and tokens not priced.
